title: Accessibility Checks We Run on Every Site
excerpt: A short, repeatable checklist that catches most of the problems real users hit.
author: Tomas Reyes
html:
Accessibility is not a final polish step. Retrofitting it is slow and expensive, and the people it affects are left waiting. We build the checks into the process so most problems never reach a client.

The automated pass

Automated tools catch roughly a third of issues: missing alt text, low contrast, unlabelled form fields and broken heading order. We run them on every pull request, and a failure blocks the merge.

The manual pass

The rest needs a human. Before every launch, one of us works through the full site with only a keyboard, then again with a screen reader. It takes about an hour and it reliably finds things the tools cannot.

  • Can every interactive element be reached and used with the keyboard alone?
  • Is the focus indicator always visible and in a logical order?
  • Do links and buttons make sense when read out of context?
  • Does the page still work at 200 percent zoom and in a narrow window?

Writing for everyone

Clear, plain language is an accessibility feature too. Short sentences, descriptive headings and meaningful link text help everybody, including the person reading on a bumpy train.

If it only works for the people who built it, it does not work yet.
